title: Batching‑aware hit‑propensity annealer: safe TTL/retention tuning and key mutation heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our current KV/prefix caching tuning is manual and largely TTL-driven. With increased batched traffic patterns and variable prefix multiplicity, static TTLs either underutilize cache (wasted GPU cycles) or oversubscribe (stale/misplaced cache pressure). This ticket scopes an automated 'annealer' that recommends and safely applies retention (TTL) and cache key mutation rules using a batching‑aware hit‑propensity model and staged rollout guarantees.

Goals:
- Produce per-prefix retention suggestions that account for batching latency/cost tradeoffs and per-route unit economics.
- Provide safe apply/rollback orchestration (dry-run, staged canary, automated revert triggers).
- Expose actionable explanations: why increase/decrease TTL, sample traffic windows, and expected token cost delta.
- Integrate with Console to show simulated P50/P95 latency and cost forecasts for proposed changes.

Success metrics (post-rollout 2 weeks):
- Token cost per 100k requests reduced >= 6% for targeted routes without >3% increase in P95 latency.
- No customer-facing errors attributable to cache policy changes (0 incidents).
- Automated rollback triggers engaged in <1% of canaries; root cause and fix checklist created.

Deliverables:
1) Hit‑propensity model: offline job that computes per-prefix P(hit | retention, batch_size, seq_len) and estimates marginal cost delta.
2) Annealer engine: picks a conservative retention ladder and proposes increments/decrements with confidence bands.
3) Safety harness: dry-run simulation, shadow replay, 5% canary cohort, automatic revert if anomaly thresholds breach.
4) Console changes: rollout UI with confidence, expected cost delta, and one-click revert.
5) Runbook: operator steps, postmortem templates, and troubleshooting queries.

Approach summary:
- Data collection: 7d of token-level logs (prefix, hash, batch_size, seq_len, hit/miss, model_variant). Use aggregation queries in ClickHouse to compute per-prefix hit curves and batch sensitivity. Stored in kv_hit_summaries.daily.
- Modeling: Fit a beta-binomial hit‑propensity model per prefix class (by entropy bucket) with batch_size interaction term. Use bootstrap to compute 95% CI for expected hit uplift when increasing TTL by N seconds.
- Simulation: Replay 48h of sampled requests against proposed retention ladders to compute cost and latency deltas under realistic batching.
- Apply logic: create an ordered plan of N safe steps where each step is a small TTL delta applied to 1) shadow namespace, 2) 0% apply with shadow traffic, 3) 5% canary (selected user cohorts or route traffic), 4) 25% ramp, 5) full apply.
- Rollback triggers: error rate spike > 0.5% above baseline, P95 latency increase > 10% for canary, or cache hit drop > 15% vs simulation. Any trigger causes immediate automated revert and page on-call.

Design doc and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.com/cost-automation/hitpropensity-annealer (draft)
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12288
- Simulation notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-ExampleNotebook
- Dashboard: Console > Cost > Annealer > Simulations (panel id: ANNEAL-7)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Conservative vs aggressive annealing: How many steps should the ladder have by default? Proposal: 5-step ladder (0%, +10%, +25%, +50%, +100% retention) with cataloged fallback when variance high.
- Canary selection: route-based vs customer-based. Route-based is faster to reason about; customer-based better isolates risk for high-profile customers. Recommend route-based by default and opt-in customer cohort canaries for enterprise routes.
- Model freshness: run nightly vs run hourly. Nightly suffices for most prefixes; allow hourly for high-volume real‑time routes.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: instrumentation and ClickHouse aggregates (ENG-900405 child)
- Week 2: model pipeline + example simulations (ENG-900406 child)
- Week 3: annealer service + dry-run mode (ENG-900407 child)
- Week 4: canary orchestration + console UI + runbook (ENG-900408 child)

Testing checklist:
- Unit tests for model and statistical bounds.
- Integration test: replay harness against a staging runtime cluster.
- Chaos test: simulate sudden prefix surge and ensure rollback triggers fire.
- Security review: verify no sensitive PII is included in retention analytics.

Notes on cache key mutation heuristics:
- Avoid canonicalizing user-associated tokens unless TTL confidence > 99% (risk of privacy/semantics).
- For high-cardinality prefixes, suggest affix coalescing (strip noise suffixes) after evaluating collision risk via top-K suffix entropy estimator.
- Provide deterministic key hashing option with shard affinity control to prevent hot‑shard amplification.

Important SQL snippets (examples to reproduce aggregates):
- Aggregate query: SELECT prefix, batch_size, count() AS requests, sum(is_hit) AS hits, quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) AS p95_lat FROM kv_logs WHERE ts >= now()-7d GROUP BY prefix, batch_size;
- Entropy estimator: SELECT prefix, approx_entropy(suffix_sample) AS suffix_entropy FROM kv_logs_sample GROUP BY prefix HAVING requests>1000;

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Simulation mismatch with production batching behavior. Mitigation: expand shadow replay sampling windows and include peak hours.
- Risk: Key canonicalization causes semantics break. Mitigation: require opt-in domain whitelist and deterministic rollback.
- Risk: Automated rollback flapping. Mitigation: implement cooldown and max revert frequency per route (1 revert per 24h default).
